scope: NtQueryVolumeInformationFile classes4 (FileFsDeviceInformation) and1 (FileFsVolumeInformation), x86 stdcall, Apple-backed virtual filesystem profile. See nt-file.json for the class1 extension.
behavior: Own a duplicated descriptor while consulting fstat/fstatfs; registry rejects invalid and wrong-type handles with separate NTSTATUS values. LastError is unchanged.

Local APFS/HFS yields FILE_DEVICE_DISK_FILE_SYSTEM (8); nfs/smbfs/afpfs yields FILE_DEVICE_NETWORK_FILE_SYSTEM (20). Native MNT_RDONLY and MNT_LOCAL determine READ_ONLY_DEVICE and REMOTE_DEVICE. No physical-drive, removable-media or mounted-disk flag is fabricated.

Success writes exactly two 32-bit device fields and IO_STATUS_BLOCK {STATUS_SUCCESS,8}; native structures remain host-owned. Both guest destinations are checked before either copy and permission changes remain excluded through both copies.

Class zero is invalid; insufficient capacity is rejected before pointers/handles. Null/wrapped buffers and non-four-byte-aligned outputs are rejected. Invalid preconditions leave both outputs unchanged.
Protected guest pointers retain the runtime abort policy, not Windows SEH recovery.
validation: Mac normal/ThreadSanitizer/checked and sole checked iPad fixture, actual descriptors and mounts, metadata-only rights, file/directory queries, borrowed lifetime, preserved file offset, CPU/stdcall/LastError and sentinel bytes.

Seven guarded stops: protected output, status block and crossing page; direct guest pointer to fstatfs; wrong native fstatfs return ABI; unimplemented class and device object. Mac shared-memory fork checks confirm neither output changed before faults.
Dynamic ntdll lookup invokes actual generated wrapper against a real file.
limits: No native Windows comparison run was available. Error precedence uses upstream Windows API tests; four-byte output alignment is inferred from the x86 structures and NT probe convention rather than a captured class-4 Windows experiment.
Virtual-volume serial/label semantics are specified in nt-file.json. No size/attributes classes, asynchronous operation or IO-completion delivery.
Only APFS/HFS local mounts were exercised. Network and read-only mount mappings are implemented from native flags but no such mounted test volume was available.
No full physical-device/NTFS/ACL equivalence; unexpected descriptor inspection failure currently returns STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL without an IOSB completion.
